theory_content: A covered call combines stock ownership with selling a call option against the same shares. It can generate premium income, but it also caps upside beyond the strike price.
A protective put pairs a long stock position with a put option. It reduces downside risk, but the option premium lowers net returns if the stock rises slowly.
Option spreads use two or more option legs to shape payoff. Vertical spreads are common because they reduce cost and define maximum risk and maximum profit.
